This page sets out what you do in the multi-day format on the Housing and racial bias case study, and where. The [background page](../../background.qmd) presents the original study and the two studies of SCORE that took it up, the robustness study with its five reanalyses [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness] and the replicability study with its new experiment, and it is the place to start if you have not read it. The first day teaches R, the IDE and Quarto in the IDE workspace of the case study, which you download and open in Positron, RStudio, VS Code or another IDE, as the [Setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) describes. The second day is the full-day format, which takes all six tasks, and you do them in the IDE workspace. The slides of that day show each step with its output, so that you can compare your numbers with them. If your installation fails, the slides, which run R inside your browser, and the [webR workspace](../../lab.qmd), a page of the workshop's website that holds the same tasks, carry the work instead and give the same numbers. On the third day the analysis that you declared in Task 5 becomes a report of your own, written in Quarto in the IDE workspace and kept under Git.

### Your report

On the third day you turn the folder of the IDE workspace into a repository, with the preregistration block that you completed in Task 5 as the first commit, and write the report around the declared analysis: the result with its uncertainty, its place on the curve of the claim, any departure from the declaration and the reason for it, and what the replication with new data adds. The page of [day 3](day-3.qmd) holds the steps.

## Links

The workshop's tools:

- [Slides](../day/slides.qmd) – the slides of the second day, which show each step with its output; the pages of the first and the third days link the slide deck of each session.
- [Setup](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) – installing R and an IDE, and downloading the IDE workspace.
- [Help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) – the problems that other participants have met, and what to do about each.
- [The IDE workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing-workspace/) – the report of the workspace as it renders, with the output of every chunk under its code.
- [webR workspace](../../lab.qmd) – the whole exercise and its data in a browser tab.
- [Cheatsheet](../../cheatsheet.qmd) – the addresses, the helpers, the reproductions of Task 3 and the quick fixes of the second day on one page.
